# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

# Official BIRD structure layer: thrombosis_prediction

## Examination
- ID integer — identification of the patient
- Examination Date date — Examination Date
- aCL IgG real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgG) concentration
- aCL IgM real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgM) concentration
- ANA integer — anti-nucleus antibody concentration
- ANA Pattern text — pattern observed in the sheet of ANA examination
- aCL IgA integer — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgA) concentration
- Diagnosis text — disease names
- KCT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- RVVT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- LAC text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- Symptoms text — other symptoms observed
- Thrombosis integer — degree of thrombosis; values: 0: negative (no thrombosis)1: positive (the most severe one)2: positive (severe)3: positive (mild)

## Patient
- ID integer — identification of the patient
- SEX text — Sex; values: F: female; M: male
- Birthday date — Birthday
- Description date — the first date when a patient data was recorded; values: null or empty: not recorded
- First Date date — the date when a patient came to the hospital
- Admission text — patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-); values: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-)
- Diagnosis text — disease names

## Laboratory

- ProfileImageUrl text — the profile image url

- UserId integer — the id of the voter

# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event

- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar

Examples of good alignments include Superman, Wonder Woman, and Spider-Man.Neutral: These superheroes may not always prioritize the greater good, but they are not necessarily evil either. They may act in their own self-interest or make decisions based on their own moral code. Examples of neutral alignments include the Hulk and Deadpool.	Bad: These superheroes are typically selfish, manipulative, and willing to harm others in pursuit of their own goals. Examples of evil alignments include Lex Luthor and the Joker.

- id integer — the unique identifier of the attribute
- attribute_name text — the attribute; values: commonsense evidence:A superhero's attribute is a characteristic or quality that defines who they are and what they are capable of. This could be a physical trait, such as superhuman strength or the ability to fly, or a personal trait, such as extraordinary intelligence or exceptional bravery.

- id integer — the unique identifier of the gender

# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

  SELECT attendance.link_to_event, COUNT(attendance.link_to_event) AS member_attendance_count
  FROM attendance
  GROUP BY attendance.link_to_event
  HAVING COUNT(attendance.link_to_event) > 10
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_event_count
FROM qualifying_events
INNER JOIN event ON qualifying_events.link_to_event = event.event_id
WHERE event.type = 'Meeting'

WITH ariel_rating AS (
  SELECT pa.overall_rating AS ariel_overall_rating
  FROM Player_Attributes AS pa
  INNER JOIN Player AS p ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  WHERE p.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk'
),
paulin_rating AS (
  SELECT pa.overall_rating AS paulin_overall_rating
  FROM Player_Attributes AS pa
  INNER JOIN Player AS p ON pa.player_api_id = p.player_api_id
  WHERE p.player_name = 'Paulin Puel'
)
SELECT (ariel_rating.ariel_overall_rating - paulin_rating.paulin_overall_rating) * 100.0 / paulin_rating.paulin_overall_rating AS percentage_higher
FROM ariel_rating
CROSS JOIN paulin_rating

SELECT s.School, s.DOCType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN frpm AS f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > (
    SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)")
    FROM schools AS s2
    JOIN frpm AS f2 ON s2.CDSCode = f2.CDSCode
    WHERE s2.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  );

WITH youngest AS (
  SELECT MAX(client.birth_date) AS max_birth
  FROM client
),
highest_salary AS (
  SELECT MAX(district.A11) AS max_salary
  FROM district
)
SELECT DISTINCT account.account_id
FROM account
INNER JOIN disp ON account.account_id = disp.account_id
INNER JOIN client ON disp.client_id = client.client_id
INNER JOIN district ON client.district_id = district.district_id
INNER JOIN youngest ON client.birth_date = youngest.max_birth
INNER JOIN highest_salary ON district.A11 = highest_salary.max_salary

SELECT a.account_id
FROM account AS a
JOIN disp AS dp ON a.account_id = dp.account_id
JOIN client AS c ON dp.client_id = c.client_id
JOIN district AS d ON c.district_id = d.district_id
WHERE c.birth_date = (SELECT MAX(birth_date) FROM client)
  AND d.A11 = (SELECT MAX(A11) FROM district);

- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

## Examination
- ID integer — identification of the patient
- Examination Date date — Examination Date
- aCL IgG real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgG) concentration
- aCL IgM real — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgM) concentration
- ANA integer — anti-nucleus antibody concentration
- ANA Pattern text — pattern observed in the sheet of ANA examination
- aCL IgA integer — anti-Cardiolipin antibody (IgA) concentration
- Diagnosis text — disease names
- KCT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- RVVT text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- LAC text — measure of degree of coagulation; values: +: positive-: negative
- Symptoms text — other symptoms observed
- Thrombosis integer — degree of thrombosis; values: 0: negative (no thrombosis)1: positive (the most severe one)2: positive (severe)3: positive (mild)

## Patient
- ID integer — identification of the patient
- SEX text — Sex; values: F: female; M: male
- Birthday date — Birthday
- Description date — the first date when a patient data was recorded; values: null or empty: not recorded
- First Date date — the date when a patient came to the hospital
- Admission text — patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-); values: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-)
- Diagnosis text — disease names

## Laboratory
- ID integer — identification of the patient
- Date date — Date of the laboratory tests (YYMMDD)
- GOT integer — AST glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 60
- GPT integer — ALT glutamic pyruvic transaminase; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 60

- T-BIL real — total bilirubin; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 2.0

- GLU integer — blood glucose; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 180

- RBC real — Red blood cell; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 3.5 < N < 6.0
- HGB real — Hemoglobin; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 10 < N < 17
- HCT real — Hematoclit; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 29 < N < 52
- PLT integer — platelet; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: 100 < N < 400
- PT real — prothrombin time; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 14
- APTT integer — activated partial prothrombin time; values: Commonsense evidence:Normal range: N < 45

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name

- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense

- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id

- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code

# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

forge.sql:
WITH attendance_counts AS (
  SELECT attendance.link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count
  FROM attendance
  GROUP BY attendance.link_to_event
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_event_count
FROM event
INNER JOIN attendance_counts ON event.event_id = attendance_counts.event_id
WHERE event.type = 'Meeting' AND attendance_counts.attendee_count > 10

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT Patient.ID) AS count_patients
FROM Patient
INNER JOIN Laboratory ON Patient.ID = Laboratory.ID
INNER JOIN Examination ON Patient.ID = Examination.ID
WHERE Laboratory.CPK < 250 AND (Examination.KCT = '+' OR Examination.RVVT = '+' OR Examination.LAC = '+')

assistant.text:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID)
FROM Patient AS p
JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
JOIN Examination AS e ON e.ID = p.ID
WHERE l.CPK < 250
  AND (e.KCT = '+' OR e.RVVT = '+' OR e.LAC = '+');

direct.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID)
FROM Patient AS p
JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID
JOIN Examination AS e ON e.ID = p.ID
WHERE l.CPK < 250
  AND (e.KCT = '+' OR e.RVVT = '+' OR e.LAC = '+')

# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

# Official BIRD structure layer: student_club

## event
- event_id text — A unique identifier for the event
- event_name text — event name
- event_date text — The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place; values: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00
- type text — The kind of event, such as game, social, election
- notes text — A free text field for any notes about the event
- location text — Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location
- status text — One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed; values: Open/ Closed/ Planning

## major
- major_id text — A unique identifier for each major
- major_name text — major name
- department text — The name of the department that offers the major
- college text — The name college that houses the department that offers the major

## zip_code
- zip_code integer — The ZIP code itself. A five-digit number identifying a US post office.
- type text — The kind of ZIP code; values: commonsense evidence: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.
- city text — The city to which the ZIP pertains
- county text — The county to which the ZIP pertains
- state text — The name of the state to which the ZIP pertains
- short_state text — The abbreviation of the state to which the ZIP pertains

## attendance
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event which was attended; values: References the Event table
- link_to_member text — The unique identifier of the member who attended the event; values: References the Member table

## budget
- budget_id text — A unique identifier for the budget entry
- category text — The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking
- spent real — The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event.; values: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table
- remaining real — A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence: If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.
- amount integer — The amount budgeted for the specified category and event; values: the unit is dollar commonsense evidence:some computation like: amount = spent + remaining
- event_status text — the status of the event; values: Closed / Open/ Planning commonsense evidence: • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore.• Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses.• Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.
- link_to_event text — The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies.; values: References the Event table

## expense
- expense_id text — unique id of income
- expense_description text — A textual description of what the money was spend for
- expense_date text — The date the expense was incurred; values: e.g. YYYY-MM-DD
- cost real — The dollar amount of the expense; values: the unit is dollar
- approved text — A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved; values: true/ false
- link_to_member text — The member who incurred the expense
- link_to_budget text — The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event.; values: References the Budget table

## income
- income_id text — A unique identifier for each record of income
- date_received text — the date that the fund received
- amount integer — amount of funds; values: the unit is dollar
- source text — A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation
- notes text — A free-text value giving any needed details about the receipt of funds
- link_to_member text — link to member

## member
- member_id text — unique id of member
- first_name text — member's first name
- last_name text — member's last name; values: commonsense evidence: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.
- email text — member's email
- position text — The position the member holds in the club
- t_shirt_size text — The size of tee shirt that member wants when shirts are ordered; values: commonsense evidence: usually the student ordered t-shirt with lager size has bigger body shape
- phone text — The best telephone at which to contact the member
- zip integer — the zip code of the member's hometown
- link_to_major text — The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table

# Foreign-key relationships
- attendance.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- attendance.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- budget.link_to_event -> event.event_id
- expense.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- expense.link_to_budget -> budget.budget_id
- income.link_to_member -> member.member_id
- member.zip -> zip_code.zip_code
- member.link_to_major -> major.major_id

forge.sql:
WITH qualifying_meetings AS (
  SELECT event.event_id
  FROM event
  INNER JOIN attendance ON event.event_id = attendance.link_to_event
  WHERE event.type = 'Meeting'
  GROUP BY event.event_id
  HAVING COUNT(attendance.link_to_member) > 10
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_count
FROM qualifying_meetings

forge.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "Patient"."ID") AS count_patients_with_positive_coagulation_and_normal_cpk
FROM Patient
INNER JOIN Laboratory ON Patient.ID = Laboratory.ID
INNER JOIN Examination ON Patient.ID = Examination.ID
WHERE Laboratory.CPK < 250 AND (Examination.KCT = '+' OR Examination.RVVT = '+' OR Examination.LAC = '+')

WITH ariel_rating AS (
  SELECT Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS rating
  FROM Player_Attributes
  INNER JOIN Player ON Player_Attributes.player_api_id = Player.player_api_id
  WHERE Player.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk'
  ORDER BY Player_Attributes.id ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
paulin_rating AS (
  SELECT Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS rating
  FROM Player_Attributes
  INNER JOIN Player ON Player_Attributes.player_api_id = Player.player_api_id
  WHERE Player.player_name = 'Paulin Puel'
  ORDER BY Player_Attributes.id ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT ((ariel_rating.rating - paulin_rating.rating) * 100.0 / paulin_rating.rating) AS percentage_higher
FROM ariel_rating
CROSS JOIN paulin_rating

SELECT (a.overall_rating - b.overall_rating) * 100.0 / b.overall_rating
FROM Player_Attributes AS a
JOIN Player AS p1 ON a.player_api_id = p1.player_api_id
CROSS JOIN Player_Attributes AS b
JOIN Player AS p2 ON b.player_api_id = p2.player_api_id
WHERE p1.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk'
  AND p2.player_name = 'Paulin Puel';

forge.sql:
WITH best AS (
  SELECT MIN(lapTimes.milliseconds) AS best_ms
  FROM lapTimes
)
SELECT lapTimes.milliseconds, drivers.forename, drivers.surname, races.name
FROM lapTimes
INNER JOIN drivers ON lapTimes.driverId = drivers.driverId
INNER JOIN races ON lapTimes.raceId = races.raceId
INNER JOIN best ON lapTimes.milliseconds = best.best_ms

WITH japanese_zero AS (
  SELECT constructors.constructorId, COUNT(constructorResults.raceId) AS race_count, SUM(constructorResults.points) AS total_points
  FROM constructors
  INNER JOIN constructorResults ON constructors.constructorId = constructorResults.constructorId
  WHERE constructors.nationality = 'Japanese'
  GROUP BY constructors.constructorId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS constructor_count
FROM japanese_zero
WHERE race_count = 2 AND total_points = 0

WHERE circuits.country = 'Austria'
GROUP BY circuits.location, circuits.lat, circuits.lng

SELECT COUNT(r.raceId) AS times_held, c.location, c.lat, c.lng
FROM circuits AS c
JOIN races AS r ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId
WHERE c.country = 'Austria'
GROUP BY c.circuitId, c.location, c.lat, c.lng;

forge.sql:
WITH stats AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_superheroes, COUNT(superhero.id) FILTER (WHERE alignment.alignment = 'Bad') AS bad_superheroes, COUNT(superhero.id) FILTER (WHERE alignment.alignment = 'Bad' AND publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics') AS bad_marvel_superheroes
  FROM superhero
  INNER JOIN alignment ON superhero.alignment_id = alignment.id
  INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_superheroes, COUNT(superhero.id) FILTER (WHERE alignment.alignment = 'Bad') AS bad_superheroes, COUNT(superhero.id) FILTER (WHERE alignment.alignment = 'Bad' AND publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics') AS bad_marvel_superheroes
FROM superhero
INNER JOIN alignment ON superhero.alignment_id = alignment.id
INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id

SELECT eye.colour AS eyes, hair.colour AS hair, skin.colour AS skin
FROM superhero AS s
INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id
INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS eye ON s.eye_colour_id = eye.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS hair ON s.hair_colour_id = hair.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS skin ON s.skin_colour_id = skin.id
WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND p.publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics'

assistant.text:
SELECT eye.colour AS eyes, hair.colour AS hair, skin.colour AS skin
FROM superhero AS s
JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id
JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id
JOIN colour AS eye ON s.eye_colour_id = eye.id
JOIN colour AS hair ON s.hair_colour_id = hair.id
JOIN colour AS skin ON s.skin_colour_id = skin.id
WHERE g.gender = 'Female'
  AND p.publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics';

FROM schools AS s
JOIN frpm AS f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode
WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > (
    SELECT AVG(f2."Enrollment (K-12)" - f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)")
    FROM schools AS s2
    JOIN frpm AS f2 ON s2.CDSCode = f2.CDSCode
    WHERE s2.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
  );

forge.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT account.account_id
FROM account
INNER JOIN disp ON account.account_id = disp.account_id
INNER JOIN client ON disp.client_id = client.client_id
INNER JOIN district ON client.district_id = district.district_id
WHERE client.birth_date = (
  SELECT MAX(client.birth_date) AS max_birth_date
  FROM client
) AND district.A11 = (
  SELECT MAX(district.A11) AS max_salary
  FROM district
)

  SELECT attendance.link_to_event AS event_id, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count

WHERE event.type = 'Meeting' AND attendance_counts.attendee_count > 10

candidates.sql:
WITH qualifying_meetings AS (
  SELECT event.event_id
  FROM event
  INNER JOIN attendance ON event.event_id = attendance.link_to_event
  WHERE event.type = 'Meeting'
  GROUP BY event.event_id
  HAVING COUNT(attendance.link_to_member) > 10
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS meeting_count
FROM qualifying_meetings

WITH ariel_rating AS (
  SELECT Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS rating
  FROM Player_Attributes
  INNER JOIN Player ON Player_Attributes.player_api_id = Player.player_api_id
  WHERE Player.player_name = 'Ariel Borysiuk'
  ORDER BY Player_Attributes.id ASC
  LIMIT 1
),
paulin_rating AS (
  SELECT Player_Attributes.overall_rating AS rating
  FROM Player_Attributes
  INNER JOIN Player ON Player_Attributes.player_api_id = Player.player_api_id
  WHERE Player.player_name = 'Paulin Puel'
  ORDER BY Player_Attributes.id ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT ((ariel_rating.rating - paulin_rating.rating) * 100.0 / paulin_rating.rating) AS percentage_higher
FROM ariel_rating
CROSS JOIN paulin_rating

INNER JOIN best ON lapTimes.milliseconds = best.best_ms

WITH japanese_zero AS (
  SELECT constructors.constructorId, COUNT(constructorResults.raceId) AS race_count, SUM(constructorResults.points) AS total_points
  FROM constructors
  INNER JOIN constructorResults ON constructors.constructorId = constructorResults.constructorId
  WHERE constructors.nationality = 'Japanese'
  GROUP BY constructors.constructorId
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS constructor_count
FROM japanese_zero
WHERE race_count = 2 AND total_points = 0

  FROM schools
  INNER JOIN frpm ON schools.CDSCode = frpm.CDSCode
  WHERE schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded'
)

FROM schools
INNER JOIN frpm ON schools.CDSCode = frpm.CDSCode

WHERE schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded' AND frpm.Enrollment (K-12) - frpm.Enrollment (Ages 5-17) > (
  SELECT avg_difference
  FROM avg_difference
)
